chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn Aamir, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, who said:

I saw Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) when he performed Sajdah, moved three fingers from his fingers, one after the other, with a slight movement as if he was counting the Glorifications, then raised his head.
ai.seo_question: How did the Imams perform the physical movements during Sajdah in prayer?
ai.summary: This narration from *Al-Kafi* details the physical etiquette of Imam Al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him), specifically his subtle movement of three fingers during prostration to count glorifications. This practice underscores the Shia emphasis on *Adab* (etiquette) and mindfulness (*Khushu*) in prayer, linking physical actions to spiritual remembrance. It serves as a practical guide for replicating the Prophet's and Imams' precise manner of worship, reinforcing the connection between bodily discipline and inner devotion.

en.hubeali: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Abdullah Bin Aamir, from Ali Bin Mahziyar, from Muhammad Bin Ismail who said,

en.sarwar: 3. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Amir from Ali ibn Mahziyar from Muhammad ibn Isma’il who has said the following: “
I saw abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, when prostrating, move three of his fingers one after the other slightly as if counting rosary and then raise his head from prostration.”
